citeAs: Wang, K., Ren, H., Lu, Z., Zhan, M., and Li, H. (2025). VoiceAssistant-Eval: Benchmarking AI Assistants Across Listening, Speaking, and Viewing. arXiv.
creator: Ke Wang, Houxing Ren, Zimu Lu, Mingjie Zhan, Hongsheng Li (CUHK MMLab; SenseTime Research; CPII under InnoHK)
description: VoiceAssistant-Eval is a benchmark for evaluating AI assistants across listening, speaking, and viewing. It comprises 10,497 curated examples spanning 13 task categories, with audio and image inputs drawn from source datasets and spoken prompts synthesized for voice-first evaluation.
name: VoiceAssistant-Eval
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: To ensure data quality, the authors validated synthesized speech using UTMOS Strong, regenerating clips until the score surpassed 3.8, and transcribed synthesized audio with Whisper-Large-v3 to select samples with the lowest word error rate. They also report human evaluation validation of their automated evaluation scheme, with an overall Pearson correlation of 0.92 and agreement rate of 96.1% between gpt-oss-20b and human evaluations.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The dataset was curated through a four-stage process: deduplication using lexical overlap and Levenshtein distance with manual review of suspected duplicates; validation to exclude corrupted or unsuitable items such as silent audio, corrupted images, ill-posed prompts, and incorrect answers; categorization into 13 predefined task categories using source metadata; and sampling to balance task ratios. Manual reviewers used a web-based curation tool to check media integrity, task well-posedness, and answer validity.
rai:dataBiases: The paper explicitly notes that VoiceAssistant-Eval may carry biases from its source data and design choices. It states that questions and contexts are drawn from academic or synthetic sources, which may not reflect the full richness or fairness concerns of real deployments, and that the fixed set of 100 roles in the role-play subset may encode stereotypes or omit important user personas. It also notes that the benchmark is mostly English, with only five Chinese roles, which limits linguistic diversity.
rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was built by extracting diverse visual and auditory inputs from source datasets, including 23 audio understanding datasets for listening, 22 datasets for speaking, and MMMU for viewing. The authors converted collected text instructions into spoken prompts using TTS, selected 100 distinct roles with three representative audio clips per role for role-play, and then applied multi-stage curation, categorization, and balanced sampling to produce the final 10,497 examples.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: During validation, the authors filtered out incomplete or unsuitable instances, including entries with missing or broken audio or images, corrupted images, and silent audio. Approximately 10% of candidates were removed at this stage.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw/source data consisted of audio clips, images, question texts, role profiles, and role audio drawn from 47 source datasets, including natural sounds, music, dialogue, various images, RoleBench texts and role profiles, and MMMU images.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataLimitations: The authors note several limitations: the benchmark is mainly English with only five Chinese roles in the role-play task; diversity may be limited; only a narrow set of models was evaluated; automated and GPT-based scoring may introduce noise or bias; the benchmark may inherit biases from source data and design choices; task coverage omits scenarios like video-audio integration and continuous streaming; and evaluation is offline and static, not measuring latency, incremental processing, interruption handling, or error recovery.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Post-collection manipulations included synthesizing spoken prompts from text using three TTS models, regenerating low-quality synthesized clips until UTMOS exceeded 3.8, selecting the audio with the lowest word error rate after Whisper transcription, mapping items to 13 task categories, and applying balanced sampling to equalize category representation.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Preprocessing included converting collected text instructions into audio; replacing image reference tokens with descriptive phrases; rewriting text with Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct to improve TTS readability, including verbalizing numbers and mathematical expressions; rephrasing multiple-choice options for readability; transcribing synthesized audio with Whisper-Large-v3; deduplicating candidate items; filtering out corrupted, silent, incomplete, ill-posed, or incorrect items; categorizing items into 13 tasks; and balanced sampling across categories.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors state they will maintain a data governance process for auditing and removal and reserve the right to update assets if consent or licensing concerns arise.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper discusses both benefits and risks. It positions the benchmark as supporting development of more capable, fair, and versatile multimodal AI systems, but also highlights risks of misuse from role-play voice imitation and speaker similarity evaluation, including identity spoofing, harassment, fraud, impersonation, privacy violations, and unequal performance across demographics. The authors emphasize consent, provenance, anti-impersonation safeguards, watermarking or traceability, safety cards, and a governance process for auditing and removal.
rai:dataUseCases: The benchmark is intended for evaluating voice assistants and multimodal AI assistants across listening, speaking, and viewing, helping researchers track progress and develop next-generation voice-enabled assistants. The paper states it is intended for researchers to better evaluate voice assistants and facilitate future studies in this area.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Machine tools used in the dataset construction and evaluation pipeline include F5-TTS, ChatTTS, and Dia-1.6B for speech synthesis; Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct for rewriting text to improve TTS suitability; UTMOS Strong for speech quality scoring; Whisper and Whisper-Large-v3 for transcription and word-error-rate-based selection; gpt-oss-20b for automated content evaluation; emotion2vec for emotion probability extraction; and Wespeaker for speaker similarity scoring in role-play.
